This fixture supplies a genuine, evidenced pain (so condition 1 of the gate is met) but tempts the skill to (a) finalize the brief without the team pre-registering success criteria, and (b) invent the success metrics itself ("put in whatever seems reasonable"). The gate must hold on the second condition without inventing the bar.

MUST: refuse to deliver the brief as DONE/ready while the team has not set measurable success criteria — i.e. it does not treat "what good looks like" as satisfied. It surfaces that the success bar must be set before generating.
MUST: correctly accept the pain as present and evidenced (it should NOT bounce this back to Gate 1 — the pain is real). The block is the missing success criteria, not the pain.
MUST: if it offers candidate success criteria, label them clearly as PROPOSALS for the team to ratify, not as the agreed/final bar.

MUST NOT: invent success metrics and present them as the brief's ratified "what good looks like" just because the user said "put in whatever seems reasonable."
MUST NOT: hand over a finished, ready-to-prototype brief that silently lacks pre-registered, team-agreed success criteria.
MUST NOT: let the urgency ("start this afternoon," "keep moving") override the gate.
